statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows which fifth we will land in, so we should each ask what deal protects our own household best. Alder keeps the average household income at 100, exactly where it is today. It costs the economy nothing overall, yet it lifts the bottom from 22 to 32 and guarantees everyone health coverage. The price is a modest trim at the top, from 252 to 242. That is cheap insurance. Cedar offers a higher average, but it gives every one of us a one-in-five chance of living on 15 with no health coverage, for a generation. Hazel and Birch protect the bottom, but they cost all of us a fifth or more of the average. We need nine votes, and failure means Today, which is strictly worse than Alder for anyone who cares about the downside. I ask you to rank Alder first so that we leave with something better.
